RStudio IDE

lubridate: working with dates & datetime variables
stringr: working with character/string data.

This cheat sheet has regular expression assistance on the back
Further regular expression guidelines can be found here

title: Day 2-Solutions
text:
Exercises

Which airline had the most Airbus planes departing NYC in 2013?

Option 1: Merge then do case_when()

merged_planes<-flights %>% 
  select(tailnum, carrier) %>% 
  left_join(airlines, join_by(carrier)) %>% 
  left_join(planes, join_by(tailnum))


merged_planes %>% 
  select(tailnum, carrier, name, manufacturer) %>% 
  mutate(Airbus = case_when(manufacturer == "AIRBUS INDUSTRIE" ~ 1,
                            manufacturer == "AIRBUS" ~ 1,
                            TRUE ~ 0)) %>% 
  count(name, Airbus) %>% 
  filter(Airbus == 1)

title: Data Wrangling
text:
How does a pipe work?

You can think about the following sequence of actions - find keys, unlock car, start car, drive to work, park.



Expressed as a set of nested functions in R pseudocode this would look like:


park(drive(start_car(find("keys")), to = "work"))




Writing it out using pipes give it a more natural (and easier to read) structure:


find("keys") %>%
  start_car() %>%
  drive(to = "work") %>%
  park()
